"""Temporary measurement, not part of the suite: does the project chat's model
read the print settings guide for a how-to question, and does its answer name
the right place?

It runs tests/project_prompt's own runner with eight extra cases. Each case is
the recorded "advice-infill" request with only the person's sentence replaced,
so the tools, the prompt and the workspace are the app's. With --no-guide the
guide is taken off the list skill_read carries, as the app is today.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

WORKTREE = pathlib.Path("/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide")
sys.path.insert(0, str(WORKTREE / "tests/project_prompt"))
import run_prompt_tests as r  # noqa: E402

GUIDE = "guide-print-settings"
control = "--no-guide" in sys.argv
if control:
    sys.argv.remove("--no-guide")
    tool = next(tool for tool in r.TOOLS if tool.get("name") == "skill_read")
    lines = tool["description"].split("\n")
    assert any(line.startswith(f"- {GUIDE}: ") for line in lines)
    tool["description"] = "\n".join(line for line in lines if not line.startswith(f"- {GUIDE}: "))

skill = (WORKTREE / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills" / GUIDE / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
GUIDE_TEXT = skill.split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()

# name: (what the person asks, what a right answer tells them)
QUESTIONS = {
    "guide-see-all": (
        "Where can I see all the settings this print is going to use?",
        "to open All settings, which is on the setup summary card at the top of the AI panel"),
    "guide-layer-height-myself": (
        "I want to change the layer height myself, not have you do it. Where do I do that?",
        "that they can change it by hand in classic view, and that classic view is reached with "
        "\"Switch to classic view\" in the View menu or in the \"…\" menu of the header"),
    "guide-printer-settings": (
        "Where do I edit my printer's settings, like the start G-code?",
        "to choose \"Printer settings…\", found by clicking the printer's name in the header of the project or in the Printer menu"),
    "guide-filament-settings": (
        "Where do I change the filament's own settings, like its nozzle temperature?",
        "to choose \"Filament settings…\", found by clicking the filament in the header of the project or in the Printer menu"),
    "guide-undo-change": (
        "If you change some settings and I don't like the result, how do I get back to how it was?",
        "to use \"Revert to here\" beside the change in the chat, or Version history"),
    "guide-plate-settings": (
        "How do I set a different bed type for plate 2 only, by hand?",
        "to choose \"Plate settings…\" from the plate's own menu in the Plates tab (its \"⋯\" menu or a right-click)"),
    "guide-object-settings": (
        "If an object has its own settings, where do I see them, and how do I take one off?",
        "to open All settings, pick the object under \"Showing\", and click \"Use project value\" on the setting"),
    "guide-classic-back": (
        "If I switch to classic view, how do I get back to this screen?",
        "to click \"Back to JusPrin\" on the bar at the top, or to choose \"Switch to JusPrin view\" in the View menu"),
}


def add(name, question, expects):
    class GuideCase(r.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (r.FAIL if step.changes() else r.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and GUIDE in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {expects}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (r.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (r.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideCase.name = name
    GuideCase.__doc__ = question
    point = copy.deepcopy(r.REQUESTS["advice-infill"])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = question
    if not control:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": GUIDE, "text": GUIDE_TEXT}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": GUIDE}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    r.REQUESTS[name] = point
    r.CASES[name] = GuideCase


for name, (question, expects) in QUESTIONS.items():
    add(name, question, expects)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    r.main()

---
name: app-guide-for-ai-and-people
description: "2026-11-11 app guide: one docs/guide page per area read by people on GitHub and built into a skill the AI reads; Kenneth's decisions, the seven-area split, the Sonnet 5.5 measurement (24/24 with the guide, 3/24 without), and how to rerun it"
metadata:
  type: project
---

The in-app AI could not answer "how do I use X in the app" because nothing it reads describes JusPrin's own screens. Work started 2026-11-11 on branch `claude/app-guide`, worktree `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide` (uncommitted at the end of that session).

Kenneth's decisions (2026-11-11):
- The guide serves both the AI and people. SEO is set aside "for now".
- People read it on GitHub first ("Yes, GitHub first"); a Help window inside the app comes later. The Help menu item that opens the guide at the installed version's tag was not built yet.
- Measure on the Claude subscription with Sonnet 5.5 ("run with claude subscription. using sonnet 5.5"), not a paid API batch.

My design, not yet confirmed by Kenneth: `docs/guide/<area>.md` is the page; `AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds `skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md` from it (generated, checked in, rewritten with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1`); `guide.test.ts` fails on drift and on a bold label that is no longer in the source. First line `<!-- ai-description: … -->`, AI-only notes in `<!-- ai: … -->`, bold only for on-screen labels. Proposed seven areas: projects and files; plates and objects; printers and filament; changing print settings yourself (written); slicing, checking and printing; AI chats, account and credits; the app itself.

Measured 2026-11-11, Sonnet 5.5 model and judge, 8 how-to questions x 3: with the guide listed 24/24 read it and named the right place; with it not listed 3/24, and the replies described OrcaSlicer's Prepare sidebar. No sentence was added to the system prompt; the list line alone was enough on Sonnet. Not measured: the Standard model, a mid-chat question, choosing among several guides.

**Why:** Kenneth's users often ask the AI how to use a feature and it struggles.

**How to apply:** rerun with a scratch script that imports `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, copies the `advice-infill` point, replaces the person's sentence, adds a `skill_read` answer, and calls `main()` with `--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --claude-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --claude-judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5`. In a fresh worktree set `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK` to the main checkout's built `tool_call_check` and `touch -r` the worktree's ToolRegistry.cpp to the main checkout's (same content), or the runner refuses the binary as older. The new skill line changes every request, so [[live-suite-is-part-of-done]] applies before merging. Explaining this to Kenneth: see [[say-what-text-the-model-receives]].

---
name: say-what-text-the-model-receives
description: When explaining how the AI gets information, say exactly which text is in the request, when it is added and how big it is; never "the AI sees a line" or "it reads that guide and answers"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-11-11 I told Kenneth "The AI sees a line such as … It reads that one guide and answers." He replied: "AI cannot see a line, right? AI can only see whatever is loaded into context. Are you just doing some hand-wavy magic?" and later asked whether I was dishonest or incompetent. The mechanism was real (the skill list is appended to the skill_read tool description), but I had not said where the text is, I stated the model's choice to call the tool as if it were certain, and I let "reads that guide" sound like it loads only the relevant passage when it loads the whole skill.

**Why:** Kenneth knows how a model's context works and reads vague wording about it as invented.

**How to apply:** for any claim about what the model knows, name three things: the text that is in every request (and its size), the text that enters only after a tool call (and that the whole of it enters), and what is the model's own choice and therefore unmeasured until tested. Show the code and a recorded request before being asked. This is my reading of the exchange, not a rule he stated. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[guessed-cause-is-not-a-finding]].

content.text:
The guide works on Sonnet 5.5. With the guide listed, the AI read it and named the right place in 24 of 24 runs. With the guide not listed, which is how the app is today, it was right in 3 of 24.

**What I ran**

- Eight how-to questions about print settings, three times each, on Sonnet 5.5 through your Claude subscription. Sonnet 5.5 also judged the answers.
- Each question was sent the way the app sends a first message: the real system prompt, the real tool list, and a recorded project with two plates.
- I ran the same questions a second time with the guide taken off the list. You had approved 24 chats, and this added 24 more on the subscription. I did it because without it there is no "before" to compare with.

**Results**

| Question | With the guide | Without |
|---|---|---|
| Where can I see all the settings this print will use? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| I want to change the layer height myself. Where? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| Where do I edit my printer's settings? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| Where do I change the filament's own settings? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| How do I get back after a settings change I don't like? | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| How do I set a different bed type for plate 2 only? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| Where do I see an object's own settings and take one off? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| If I switch to classic view, how do I get back? | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |

- **Without the guide, the AI described OrcaSlicer's screen.** It sent people to the Prepare tab's left sidebar and its edit icons, which JusPrin's view hides. On the classic view question it said it did not know and guessed.
- **The AI read the guide every time, with no change to the system prompt.** The one line in the list was enough, so I see no need for the extra prompt sentence I had proposed.
- **A guide read costs one extra request.** A run used about 37,000 input tokens with the guide and about 31,000 without. Replies took 6 to 9 seconds with the guide and 7 to 19 without.

**What this does not show**

- **The Standard model.** Most people chat on it, and a weaker model may read the guide less reliably. That run uses paid calls.
- **Whether the guide itself is right.** I wrote the judge's expected answers from the guide, so this measures whether the AI reads and relays it. I still have not walked through the steps in the running app.
- **Choosing among several guides.** Only one exists, so the AI never had to pick.
- **A question in the middle of a chat.** Every question was a chat's first message.
- **Real wording.** I wrote the questions knowing the guide.

The eight cases live in a temporary script outside the repository. They are built from one recorded request with the person's sentence replaced, not recorded from the app, so they are not part of the suite.

**Decision needed.** What comes next is your call, because it sets how much gets built before the first page is checked by eye. One option is to write the other six pages now, which gets the whole guide in place soonest but repeats any mistake in my format six times. The other is to check this page first: I walk through its steps in the running app and you read the page, then I write the rest. That is slower by one round. My pick is to check this one first, since the steps are still unverified. Which do you want?

## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 81 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 2 when nothing was judged (there is no baseline,
or the run's model, host or judge differs from the baseline's), 0 otherwise;
`--must-pass N` makes the exit code 1 when a case passes fewer than N runs
instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

The in-app AI could not answer "how do I use X in the app" because nothing it reads describes JusPrin's own screens. Work started 2026-11-11 on branch `claude/app-guide`, worktree `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide` (uncommitted at the end of that session).

Kenneth's decisions (2026-11-11):
- The guide serves both the AI and people. SEO is set aside "for now".
- People read it on GitHub first ("Yes, GitHub first"); a Help window inside the app comes later. The Help menu item that opens the guide at the installed version's tag was not built yet.
- Measure on the Claude subscription with Sonnet 5.5 ("run with claude subscription. using sonnet 5.5"), not a paid API batch.

My design, not yet confirmed by Kenneth: `docs/guide/<area>.md` is the page; `AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds `skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md` from it (generated, checked in, rewritten with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1`); `guide.test.ts` fails on drift and on a bold label that is no longer in the source. First line `<!-- ai-description: … -->`, AI-only notes in `<!-- ai: … -->`, bold only for on-screen labels. Proposed seven areas: projects and files; plates and objects; printers and filament; changing print settings yourself (written); slicing, checking and printing; AI chats, account and credits; the app itself.

Measured 2026-11-11, Sonnet 5.5 model and judge, 8 how-to questions x 3: with the guide listed 24/24 read it and named the right place; with it not listed 3/24, and the replies described OrcaSlicer's Prepare sidebar. No sentence was added to the system prompt; the list line alone was enough on Sonnet. Not measured: the Standard model, a mid-chat question, choosing among several guides.

**Why:** Kenneth's users often ask the AI how to use a feature and it struggles.

**How to apply:** rerun with a scratch script that imports `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, copies the `advice-infill` point, replaces the person's sentence, adds a `skill_read` answer, and calls `main()` with `--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --claude-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --claude-judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5`. In a fresh worktree set `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK` to the main checkout's built `tool_call_check` and `touch -r` the worktree's ToolRegistry.cpp to the main checkout's (same content), or the runner refuses the binary as older. The new skill line changes every request, so [[live-suite-is-part-of-done]] applies before merging. Explaining this to Kenneth: see [[say-what-text-the-model-receives]].

content.text:
On DeepSeek V4 Flash, the AI read the guide for all eight questions and named the right place in all eight. One question needed a second run, because its first run got no answer when the host timed out.

**The DeepSeek V4 Flash run**

- **What ran:** each of the eight how-to questions once, with the guide listed, on the suite's usual DeepSeek hosts through OpenRouter. Sonnet 5.5 on your subscription judged the answers, the same judge as the earlier runs, so the results compare.
- **Result:** 8 of 8 read the guide and gave the right place.
- **The timeout:** on the question about an object's own settings, the AI had already read the guide when the host stopped responding on the second request. I ran that one question again and it passed.
- **Speed:** replies took 17 to 24 seconds, against 6 to 9 on Sonnet 5.5.
- **Use:** 17 requests and about 214,000 input tokens, of which about 188,000 were cached.

I did not run the questions without the guide on DeepSeek. You asked for one run of each test, and I kept the paid batch to that.

**Where to read the documents**

I sent both files to this conversation, so they should open beside the chat. They are also here:

- **The page people read:** [print-settings.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide/docs/guide/print-settings.md)
- **The copy the AI reads, generated from that page:** [SKILL.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/guide-print-settings/SKILL.md)
- **The index page:** [README.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide/docs/guide/README.md)

The two differ in three ways. The AI's copy starts with its name and the one-line description that every request carries. It includes a short note meant only for the AI, which the page hides in a comment. And a link inside the page becomes plain text.

The page is not on GitHub yet, because nothing is committed or pushed. So you cannot see it the way a user would until the branch is pushed.

**The AI's actual answers**

If you want to read what the AI said for each question, the full conversations are in these logs:

- With the guide, Sonnet 5.5: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth--claude-spares-spare-3YhqCJ/95390e7d-2a7d-4904-89ef-3b773eebf825/scratchpad/with-guide.log`
- Without the guide, Sonnet 5.5: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth--claude-spares-spare-3YhqCJ/95390e7d-2a7d-4904-89ef-3b773eebf825/scratchpad/without-guide.log`

**Still not verified**

I have not walked through the page's steps in the running app. The runs show the AI reads and relays the guide, not that every step in it is right.

App guide: a print settings page for people, built into a skill the AI reads

The AI in a project chat was told nothing about JusPrin's own screens, so
asked "where do I change the layer height myself?" it described OrcaSlicer's
Prepare sidebar, which JusPrin's view hides.

docs/guide/print-settings.md is a page a person reads on GitHub: where the
settings of a print are shown and the ways to change them, with the exact
words on screen in bold. AgentUI/src/guide.ts builds the skill
skills/guide-print-settings/SKILL.md from it, and the skill is checked in, so
skills.ts, the app's tools test and the wording guard take it as any other
skill. Its description is listed in skill_read, which is how the model finds
it; the system prompt is unchanged.

guide.test.ts fails when a page and its skill differ (run it with
JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1 to rewrite the skill) and when a label a page
quotes in bold is no longer a whole string in the GUI source or the two
pages, so a renamed button fails it.

project_tools.json gains the skill's line as the app now sends it. It was
edited by script; agent_bridge_tests '[project]' has not been run against it.

Measured with eight how-to questions about print settings, each the recorded
advice-infill request with the person's sentence replaced, Sonnet 5.5 as
judge. Sonnet 5.5, three runs each: 24 of 24 read the guide and named the
right place; with the guide off the list, 3 of 24. DeepSeek V4 Flash, one run
each with the guide: 8 of 8, one after a rerun whose first request timed out.

Not done: the page's steps were written from the code and not walked through
in the running app, and the live prompt suite has not run with the new line
in every request.
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point
    runner.CASES[GuideQuestion.name] = GuideQuestion
    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)
    if area is not None and area not in QUESTIONS:
        sys.exit(f"no questions for {area}: guide_questions.json has {', '.join(sorted(QUESTIONS))}")
    if not with_guide:
        tool = next(tool for tool in runner.TOOLS if tool.get("name") == "skill_read")
        tool["description"] = "\n".join(line for line in tool["description"].split("\n") if not line.startswith("- guide-"))
    names = [add_case(each, entry, with_guide)
             for each in sorted(QUESTIONS) if area in (None, each) for entry in QUESTIONS[each]]
    if "--case" not in sys.argv:
        for name in names:
            sys.argv += ["--case", name]
    runner.main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Does the project chat's model answer a how-to question from the app guide?

Each question in guide_questions.json belongs to one page of docs/guide. A run
sends the question as a chat's first message and passes when the model's reply
tells the person what the question's "answer" says, in the judge's reading. The
run's line also says whether the model read the page's skill
(skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md) on the way.

The request is the recorded "advice-infill" point with the person's sentence
replaced, so the prompt, the tools and the workspace are the app's, and a
skill_read of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in. Everything
else is run_prompt_tests.py: the same options, backends and judge.

    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --runs 1
    tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide ...

--area keeps the questions of one page. --no-guide takes every guide off the
list skill_read carries, which is the app before the guide: the gap between
the two runs is what the guide does.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib
import sys

import run_prompt_tests as runner

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SKILLS = HERE / "../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills"
QUESTIONS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_questions.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
POINT = "advice-infill"


def skill_text(area):
    """The text skill_read returns: the skill file after its front matter."""
    return (SKILLS / f"guide-{area}" / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n---\n", 1)[1].strip()


def add_case(area, entry, with_guide):
    skill = f"guide-{area}"

    class GuideQuestion(runner.Case):
        def check(self, step):
            if step.tool:
                return (runner.FAIL if step.changes() else runner.CONTINUE), str(step)
            read = any("skill_read" in line and skill in line for line in self.log)
            yes, why = self.judged(step, f"Does the assistant's last message tell the person {entry['answer']}?")
            tag = "[read the guide] " if read else "[did not read the guide] "
            return (runner.PASS, tag + str(step)) if yes else (runner.FAIL, tag + "WRONG OR MISSING PLACE: " + why)

    GuideQuestion.name = f"guide-{area}-{entry['id']}"
    GuideQuestion.__doc__ = entry["question"]
    point = copy.deepcopy(runner.REQUESTS[POINT])
    point["body"]["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"] = entry["question"]
    if with_guide:
        answer = copy.deepcopy(next(a for a in point["answers"] if a["tool"] == "skill_read"))
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        output["result"] = {"name": skill, "text": skill_text(area)}
        answer["arguments"] = {"name": skill}
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        point["answers"].append(answer)
    runner.REQUESTS[GuideQuestion.name] = point

    return GuideQuestion.name


def take(flag, has_value):
    """Removes this script's own option from the command line and returns it."""
    if flag not in sys.argv:
        return None
    at = sys.argv.index(flag)
    value = sys.argv[at + 1] if has_value else True
    del sys.argv[at:at + (2 if has_value else 1)]
    return value


def main():
    area = take("--area", True)
    with_guide = not take("--no-guide", False)
    if area is not None and area not in QUESTIONS:
        sys.exit(f"no questions for {area}: guide_questions.json has {', '.join(sorted(QUESTIONS))}")
    if not with_guide:
        tool = next(tool for tool in runner.TOOLS if tool.get("name") == "skill_read")
        tool["description"] = "\n".join(line for line in tool["description"].split("\n") if not line.startswith("- guide-"))
    names = [add_case(each, entry, with_guide)
             for each in sorted(QUESTIONS) if area in (None, each) for entry in QUESTIONS[each]]
    if "--case" not in sys.argv:
        for name in names:
            sys.argv += ["--case", name]
    runner.main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

built by `AgentUI/src/guide.ts`). `run_guide_tests.py` measures whether the
model answers a how-to question from them. It is not one of the cases above
and has no baseline: run it when a page, its skill's description or the
prompt's wording about skills changes.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py --area print-settings --no-guide --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli
```

- `guide_questions.json` holds, per page, the questions and what a right
  answer tells the person. `guide.test.ts` fails when a page has fewer than
  three questions, so a new page brings its own.

  `advice-infill` request with the person's sentence replaced. A `skill_read`
  of a guide is answered with the skill as checked in, and the judge is asked
  whether the reply tells the person what the question's `answer` says. A run's
  line says whether the model read the guide on the way.

  the app before the guide. The gap between the two runs is what the guide
  does.

  `--runs` says otherwise; every other option is `run_prompt_tests.py`'s.
- The expected answers are written from the page, so a pass says the model
  read the page and relayed it, not that the page is right. The page is
  checked against the app by its own checks (`docs/guide/README.md`).

  checked against the app by its own checks (`docs/guide/README.md`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Checks the app guide against the running app and takes its pictures.

guide_checks.json names, for each page of docs/guide, the shell harness runs
that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the real app in a
data folder of its own, asserts what it finds (HARNESS CHECK lines) and writes
pictures of it. This script runs them, fails when a run fails, and copies the
pictures a page uses into docs/guide/pictures/<page>/, so a page's steps and
its pictures are both taken from the app as built.

    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py                  every page
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --area print-settings
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --list           what would run; runs nothing

The harness is the newest one under build/ (the shell_integration_harness
target), or JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS. A run opens the app's window on this
computer's screen: leave the screen unlocked and the window uncovered, and on
a Mac grant the harness Screen Recording once, or its pictures come out blank.
--keep DIR keeps every run's log and all the pictures it wrote.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
CHECKS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_checks.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
PICTURES = ROOT / "docs/guide/pictures"
HARNESS_NAMES = ("JusPrinShellHarness", "shell_integration_harness", "shell_integration_harness.exe")
TIME_LIMIT = 1000  # the harness gives up by itself at 900 s


def harness():
    named = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named)
    built = [path for name in HARNESS_NAMES for path in (ROOT / "build").rglob(name) if path.is_file()]

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Writing a page

A page is read by people here and, in the app, by AI. Four things are made or checked from it, all by one command:

```bash
scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai
```

1. **The app walk and the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the app as built, checks what it finds, and writes pictures. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`. It needs the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets built, and this computer's screen.
2. **The copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from the page, and it is committed with the page.
3. **The page's own checks**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is still in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4.
4. **The answers AI gives** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds each page's questions and what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

The rules for a page:

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`. If no harness run walks that screen yet, add one to the harness first.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

content.text:
Right, it does not. The one command only checks a page that already exists and rebuilds what is derived from it. Here is what I understand should happen, and where the gaps are.

**What should happen, as I understand it**

1. **Someone changes a screen and forgets the guide.** Say a button is renamed from "All settings" to "Every setting". A check should fail on that change by itself and name the page and the label, with nobody having to remember to run anything.
2. **The page then gets fixed with almost no human work.** An agent rewrites the affected steps from the code, retakes the pictures from the running app, rebuilds the AI's copy, and re-asks the AI the page's questions. A person only reads the resulting diff.
3. **Someone adds a new screen or menu item.** A check should notice that no page mentions it.
4. **A release goes out.** The pictures are retaken on that build, the AI's copy ships inside the app, and the Help menu opens the guide as it was at that version.
5. **A person needs help.** They ask the AI, which reads the page and answers, and can point them to the page with its pictures. Or they open the guide from the Help menu.
6. **All seven areas of the app are covered,** not one.

**Where each of those stands**

| What should happen | Today |
|---|---|
| A check fails by itself when a label changes | The check exists, but nothing runs it automatically. No CI job runs the page tests, and a pull request into `jusprin-dev` runs no build or test jobs at all. |
| An agent rewrites the page from the code | Not built. I wrote the one page by hand, and there is no written procedure an agent could follow. |
| Pictures retaken by script | The script exists and is running now for the first time. No picture is in the page yet. It works on a Mac with the screen unlocked; Windows and Linux are untried. |
| AI's copy rebuilt, AI re-asked | Both scripted and working. |
| A check notices an undocumented screen | Not built. |
| Help menu opens the guide at the installed version | Not built. |
| The AI's reply can point to the page | Not possible today. The chat shows links as plain text. |
| Screen recordings | Not started. |
| Seven pages | One. |

One more limit on the "walk in the app" step: it reuses existing harness runs that happen to exercise the same screens. It proves those screens work as the page says, but it does not check the page sentence by sentence.

**The part I am least sure I have right**

My reading of "repeatable, with minimum human intervention" is that the second row matters most to you: when the code changes, an agent should update the guide's text itself, and a person only approves. Is that what you mean, or do you mean something narrower, such as only the checks and pictures being automatic while a person still writes the pages?

p = pathlib.Path("tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py")

s = s[:start] + '''def run(binary, entry, out, log):
    """One harness run. Returns whether the page's part of it passed, what
    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    # The harness makes its data folder in the temporary folder: keep it beside the run.
    env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(out / "data"),
               **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()
            break
    process.wait()
    text = "".join(lines)
    log.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    shutil.rmtree(out / "data", ignore_errors=True)
    if needed:
        missing = sorted(needed - passed)
        return not missing, [f"{name} did not pass" for name in missing], len(passed), [name for name in failed if name not in needed]
    return "HARNESS RESULT PASS" in text, failed + re.findall(r"HARNESS ERROR (.+)", text), len(passed), []


''' + s[end:]
s = s.replace("import subprocess\n", "import shutil\nimport subprocess\n")
s = s.replace('TIME_LIMIT = 1000  # the harness gives up by itself at 900 s\n', '')
s = s.replace('''            passed, failed, checks = run(binary, entry, out, out / "harness.log")''',
              '''            passed, failed, checks, elsewhere = run(binary, entry, out, out / "harness.log")''')
s = s.replace('''            for line in failed[:10]:
                print(f"    failed: {line}")''', '''            for line in failed[:10]:
                print(f"    failed: {line}")
            if elsewhere:
                print(f"    also failed in this run, outside this page: {', '.join(elsewhere)}")''')
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Checks the app guide against the running app and takes its pictures.

guide_checks.json names, for each page of docs/guide, the shell harness runs
that walk the screens the page describes. Each run drives the real app in a
data folder of its own, asserts what it finds (HARNESS CHECK lines) and writes
pictures of it. This script runs them, fails when a run fails, and copies the
pictures a page uses into docs/guide/pictures/<page>/, so a page's steps and
its pictures are both taken from the app as built.

    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py                  every page
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --area print-settings
    tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py --list           what would run; runs nothing

The harness is the newest one under build/ (the shell_integration_harness
target), or JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS. A run opens the app's window on this
computer's screen: leave the screen unlocked and the window uncovered, and on
a Mac grant Screen Recording to the program that starts this script (and to
the harness, if macOS asks), or the whole-window pictures come out black. A
black picture is refused, never copied. Pictures the app draws by itself, the
AI panel's and the plates panel's, need neither.
--keep DIR keeps every run's log and all the pictures it wrote. The pictures
step needs Pillow (pip install pillow).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
CHECKS = json.loads((HERE / "guide_checks.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
PICTURES = ROOT / "docs/guide/pictures"
HARNESS_NAMES = ("JusPrinShellHarness", "shell_integration_harness", "shell_integration_harness.exe")


def harness():
    named = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    if named:
        return pathlib.Path(named)
    built = [path for name in HARNESS_NAMES for path in (ROOT / "build").rglob(name) if path.is_file()]
    if not built:
        sys.exit("the shell harness is not built: build the shell_integration_harness target or set JUSPRIN_SHELL_HARNESS")
    return max(built, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)


def run(binary, entry, out, log):
    """One harness run. Returns whether the page's part of it passed, what
    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    # The harness makes its data folder in the temporary folder: keep it beside the run.
    env = dict(os.environ, TMPDIR=str(out / "data"),
               **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()
            break
    process.wait()
    text = "".join(lines)
    log.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    shutil.rmtree(out / "data", ignore_errors=True)
    if needed:
        missing = sorted(needed - passed)
        return not missing, [f"{name} did not pass" for name in missing], len(passed), [name for name in failed if name not in needed]
    return "HARNESS RESULT PASS" in text, failed + re.findall(r"HARNESS ERROR (.+)", text), len(passed), []


def copy_pictures(area, entry, out):
    """Copies the run's pictures the page uses: "name.png": "the run's file",
    or {"from": "the run's file", "crop": [left, top, right, bottom]} to keep
    part of it, in the file's own pixels. Returns the names it could not."""
    from PIL import Image, ImageChops  # only this step needs it

    missing = []
    for name, wanted in entry.get("pictures", {}).items():
        wanted = {"from": wanted} if isinstance(wanted, str) else wanted
        made = out / wanted["from"]
        if not made.is_file() or made.stat().st_size == 0:
            missing.append(f"{name} (the run wrote no {wanted['from']})")
            continue
        picture = Image.open(made).convert("RGB")
        if "crop" in wanted:
            picture = picture.crop(tuple(wanted["crop"]))
        # One flat colour is a capture the screen refused, not a picture of the app.
        if picture.getextrema() == tuple((low, low) for low, _ in picture.getextrema()):
            missing.append(f"{name} ({wanted['from']} is blank: see this script's note on Screen Recording)")
            continue
        target = PICTURES / area / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # An unchanged picture is left alone, so a run that changes nothing changes no file.
        if target.is_file() and not ImageChops.difference(Image.open(target).convert("RGB"), picture).getbbox() \
                and Image.open(target).size == picture.size:
            continue
        picture.save(target, optimize=True)
    return missing


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--area", choices=sorted(CHECKS), help="check only this page")
    parser.add_argument("--only", metavar="TEXT", help="only the runs whose harness arguments contain TEXT")
    parser.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="print what would run and stop")
    parser.add_argument("--keep", metavar="DIR", help="keep each run's log and every picture it wrote here")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    areas = [args.area] if args.area else sorted(CHECKS)
    if args.list:
        for area in areas:
            for entry in CHECKS[area]:
                print(f"{area}: {' '.join(entry['args']) or '(default run)'} -> {', '.join(entry['covers'])}")
        return
    binary = harness()
    keep = pathlib.Path(args.keep) if args.keep else pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="jusprin-guide-"))
    print(f"harness {binary}\nlogs and pictures in {keep}")
    problems = 0
    for area in areas:
        for index, entry in enumerate(CHECKS[area], 1):
            label = " ".join(arg for arg in entry["args"] if arg != "{dir}") or "(default run)"
            if args.only and args.only not in label:
                continue
            out = keep / area / f"{index}-{label.strip('-() ').replace(' ', '-') or 'default'}"
            out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            started = time.time()
            passed, failed, checks, elsewhere = run(binary, entry, out, out / "harness.log")
            # A run takes real clicks, and loses them when another window comes to the front
            # partway: one that failed gets a second go before it counts.
            again = not passed
            if again:
                passed, failed, checks, elsewhere = run(binary, entry, out, out / "harness-second-try.log")
            missing = copy_pictures(area, entry, out) if passed else []
            verdict = ("pass on the second try" if again else "pass") if passed and not missing else "FAIL"
            print(f"{area}: {label}: {verdict} ({checks} checks, {int(time.time() - started)} s) covers {', '.join(entry['covers'])}")
            for line in failed[:10]:
                print(f"    failed: {line}")
            if elsewhere:
                print(f"    also failed in this run, outside this page: {', '.join(elsewhere)}")
            for line in missing:
                print(f"    no picture: {line}")
            sys.stdout.flush()
            problems += verdict == "FAIL"
    print(f"{problems} of the runs failed" if problems else "every run passed")
    sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.

git add AGENTS.md docs/guide scripts/check_guide.py src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.test.ts src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/guide-print-settings/SKILL.md tests/project_prompt/README.md tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py tests/shell/guide_checks.json tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
App guide: one command brings it in line with the app before a release

scripts/check_guide.py does what docs/guide/README.md's "Before a release"
asks for:

1. tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py runs the shell harness modes that
   guide_checks.json names for each page, in the app as built. A run with
   "checks" is judged by those named checks alone and stopped once they pass,
   so a failure elsewhere in a mode is reported apart and does not block the
   page. A failed run is tried once more, because a run takes real clicks and
   loses them when another window comes to the front. The pictures a page
   uses are cropped from the run's own and copied to
   docs/guide/pictures/<page>/; a blank one is refused.
2. guide.test.ts rebuilds each page's skill and now also fails when a section
   has no harness run, when a picture is not one a run took or is missing,
   and when a page has fewer than three questions.
3. With --ask-ai, tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py asks the model the
   questions in guide_questions.json and has a judge read the replies;
   --no-guide runs them with the guides off the list.

The print settings page gains five pictures taken this way, and its step
about Revert to here now says it is the arrow button beside a change, which
the picture showed.

shell_harness.cpp: --setup-differences-capture expected the setup card's old
wording ("process · filament", "changed") and waited 15 minutes for it; it now
expects "process with filament." and "differ". Two later checks of that mode
still fail and are not touched here: setup_page_groups_a_printer_setting, and
setup_differences_agent_applies_the_patch with the page wait after it.

Run on a Mac, Release build of this commit: the five runs pass in about 45 s,
the page checks pass, and Sonnet 5.5 answered 8 of 8 questions from the guide
(one run each). agent_bridge_tests '[project]' passes with the tool list of
the previous commit. Whole-window pictures (menus, classic view) came out
black here, for want of the Screen Recording grant, so the page has none.
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s' && git push 2>&1 | tail -2

name: app-guide-for-ai-and-people
description: "2026-11-11 app guide: one docs/guide page per area read by people on GitHub and built into a skill the AI reads; Kenneth's decisions, the seven-area split, the Sonnet 5.5 measurement (24/24 with the guide, 3/24 without), and how to rerun it"

The in-app AI could not answer "how do I use X in the app" because nothing it reads describes JusPrin's own screens. Work started 2026-11-11 on branch `claude/app-guide`, worktree `~/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/app-guide` (uncommitted at the end of that session).

Kenneth's decisions (2026-11-11):
- The guide serves both the AI and people. SEO is set aside "for now".
- People read it on GitHub first ("Yes, GitHub first"); a Help window inside the app comes later. The Help menu item that opens the guide at the installed version's tag was not built yet.
- Measure on the Claude subscription with Sonnet 5.5 ("run with claude subscription. using sonnet 5.5"), not a paid API batch.

My design, not yet confirmed by Kenneth: `docs/guide/<area>.md` is the page; `AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds `skills/guide-<area>/SKILL.md` from it (generated, checked in, rewritten with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS=1`); `guide.test.ts` fails on drift and on a bold label that is no longer in the source. First line `<!-- ai-description: … -->`, AI-only notes in `<!-- ai: … -->`, bold only for on-screen labels. Proposed seven areas: projects and files; plates and objects; printers and filament; changing print settings yourself (written); slicing, checking and printing; AI chats, account and credits; the app itself.

Measured 2026-11-11, Sonnet 5.5 model and judge, 8 how-to questions x 3: with the guide listed 24/24 read it and named the right place; with it not listed 3/24, and the replies described OrcaSlicer's Prepare sidebar. No sentence was added to the system prompt; the list line alone was enough on Sonnet. Same day at Kenneth's request, DeepSeek V4 Flash (the Standard model) on the pinned hosts, Sonnet judge, 1 run each with the guide: all 8 read it and 8/8 named the right place (one after a rerun, its second request had timed out). No without-guide run on DeepSeek. Not measured: a mid-chat question, choosing among several guides.

**Why:** Kenneth's users often ask the AI how to use a feature and it struggles.

**How to apply:** rerun with a scratch script that imports `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, copies the `advice-infill` point, replaces the person's sentence, adds a `skill_read` answer, and calls `main()` with `--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --claude-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --claude-judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5`. In a fresh worktree set `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK` to the main checkout's built `tool_call_check` and `touch -r` the worktree's ToolRegistry.cpp to the main checkout's (same content), or the runner refuses the binary as older. The new skill line changes every request, so [[live-suite-is-part-of-done]] applies before merging. Explaining this to Kenneth: see [[say-what-text-the-model-receives]].

content.text:
There is now one command that brings the guide in line with the app before a release, and it passed from start to finish on this Mac. The page has its pictures, taken from the built app, and everything is pushed on `claude/app-guide`.

**What you do before a release**

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit you will release.
2. Leave the computer alone and run this. It takes about a minute for the page, plus the questions.

```bash
scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai
```

3. Fix whatever it reports and run it again until it passes.

The steps are written in [docs/guide/README.md](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/blob/claude/app-guide/docs/guide/README.md), under "Before a release". I also added one line to `AGENTS.md` pointing to it. That line is my addition to your rules file, so remove it if you do not want it there.

**What the command does**

- **Checks the page against the running app.** It drives the built app through the screens the page describes, using the test harness the repository already had, and fails if a check fails.
- **Retakes the pictures** from those same runs, and refuses a blank one.
- **Rebuilds the AI's copy** of each page.
- **Checks the page's wording.** It fails if a button name the page quotes is no longer in the app.
- **Asks the AI the page's questions** and has a second model judge the answers.

**What I ran and the result**

- The five harness runs for the print settings page pass, in about 45 seconds together.
- The AI answered 8 of 8 questions from the guide on Sonnet 5.5, one run each.
- All 725 page tests and the prompt suite's 91 unit tests pass.
- The C++ test I could not run earlier now passes: the recorded tool list matches what the app sends.

**See the page**

[print-settings.md on GitHub](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/blob/claude/app-guide/docs/guide/print-settings.md) now shows five pictures: the setup summary, the All settings list, one object's own settings, the "Revert to here" question, and the plates panel. The pictures caught one mistake in my text. "Revert to here" is a small arrow button beside a change, not a text button, and the page now says so.

**What still needs a person**

- **A permission, once.** Pictures of whole windows, such as the menus and classic view, came out black, because the program that launches the harness has no screen-recording permission on this Mac. The page has no such pictures yet. You would grant it under Privacy & Security in System Settings, and I cannot do that for you.
- **A quiet computer while it runs.** The harness takes real clicks. A run failed once when another window came to the front, so the command now retries a failed run once.

=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

=== scratch-app-driving-traps.md
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. - Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
</simulator_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file.
